header: Date: 2028-01-09 | Start: 16:00 UTC | Duration: 48m | Attendees: Samir Patel, Claire Wong (Redwood) — Lena Ortiz, Marcus Hale, Priya Anand (Magneto Studios)
summary: Intro discovery focusing on PLG self-serve onramp (TTFT), and tradeoffs between Hosted, Dedicated, and Private deployments. Magneto is evaluating time-to-first-token for a prototype, compliance (SOC2, SSO, KMS), and expected peak throughput. Agreed to provide security docs, free credits, and run a benchmark session next week.
topics: PLG / self-serve quickstart and TTFT expectations
Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private (VPC) tradeoffs
Security/compliance: SOC2, SSO, KMS, audit logs
Performance: latency targets, batching, KV cache
transcript:
[00:00] Samir Patel: Hey everyone, thanks for joining, we wanted to run through how quickly your team can get to first call with Redwood and then, uh, talk about deployment options.
[00:12] Lena Ortiz: Thanks Samir. We're trying to get an internal prototype in front of product by end of month — main questions are how fast can devs hit the API and what are the privacy options, like VPC or on-prem.
[00:25] Claire Wong: Totally. Our self-serve flow can get a developer to first token in under an hour if they follow the quickstart — we also provision free credits so you can run a small check. Do you already have an SSO / SAML provider?
[00:36] Priya Anand: Yes, we use Okta. Also need to know about KMS integration and data retention — we process some PII in prompts.
[00:45] Samir Patel: Okta's supported, and we have integrations for customer-managed KMS for Private installs. For Hosted we do encrypt at rest and in transit, but if you need keys customer-side that's a Private deployment.
[00:56] Marcus Hale: Can you spell out the cost/latency tradeoffs — we want responsive UX for customers, but cost is tight for a prototype.
[01:05] Claire Wong: Sure — Hosted is fastest for TTFT and easiest to iterate on, but Dedicated gives predictable throughput and lower unit cost at scale. Private (VPC/on-prem) is the most locked-down for security. For latency, it depends on model size and batching. With our runtime, short-context chat payloads can be sub-100ms per token on the right GPU; for larger sequences you're in the few hundred ms range.
[01:28] Lena Ortiz: When you say "sub-100ms" is that measured tail latency or p50? We need p95 under 300ms for the product feature.
[01:37] Claire Wong: Good clarification — that's p50. p95 will be higher; with Dedicated and proper autoscaling you can target p95 under 300ms for smaller models. We'll share specific profiles.
[01:48] Marcus Hale: What about prefix KV caching you mentioned in docs — how much does that help for repeated prompts?
[01:55] Claire Wong: Prefix/KV caching can cut token compute a lot for repeated contexts — it's particularly effective for assistants with stable system prompts. For evaluation we'll show a sample where effective tokens/session drop by ~30–50%.
[02:10] Priya Anand: For compliance, do you provide audit logs per request? We need to keep traceability for 12 months.
[02:17] Samir Patel: Yes, audit logs and request-level metadata are available; extended retention is an add-on for enterprise packages and is included in Private deployments. We'll bundle the audit log spec in the security pack.
[02:27] Lena Ortiz: How does the quickstart work for our devs? Can we give access to product engineers without a sales call?
[02:33] Samir Patel: Absolutely — we do PLG self-serve. We'll provision 60k credits and invite up to five devs. They sign up, grab an API key, and follow the repo quickstart. Claire, do you want to add something about SDKs?
[02:44] Claire Wong: Yeah — SDKs for Node/Python, examples for streaming, function call patterns — most teams hit first call in 20–45 minutes if they run the sample. If the prompt set is complex we'll help with prompt engineering patterns too.
[02:58] Marcus Hale: If we outgrow credits and hit higher qps, what's the path?
[03:03] Samir Patel: Typically teams move from Hosted credits to either Dedicated reserved capacity or a Private pilot. Dedicated is good for production with SLA, Private is for strict data residency or KMS needs. We can model cost for expected qps.
[03:15] Priya Anand: Any gotchas with VPC connecting? Our infra team uses strict outbound rules.
[03:21] Claire Wong: For VPC we do a customer-managed control plane and require either a peered VPC or private link. There are networking docs; sometimes customers need firewall rule whitelisting for egress during setup. We'll include a network checklist.
[03:35] Lena Ortiz: Can we run a benchmark with a small dataset to compare Dedicated vs Hosted for latency and cost?
[03:40] Claire Wong: Yes — we'll run a short benchmark during the follow-up with your sample prompts. If you can share sample prompt list and expected concurrency we'll size the GPU and estimate cost.
[03:53] Marcus Hale: Also curious about model variants — can Redwood route to cheaper quantized variants automatically if load spikes?
[03:59] Samir Patel: Yes we have model variants and automatic fallback routing — policy-based routing can cut cost during spikes while preserving a fallback for higher-quality models. We'll show a routing policy example.
[04:12] (crosstalk) Priya Anand: One more — retention of user-submitted content. For Hosted is there a way to auto-delete logs?
[04:18] Samir Patel: Hosted has configurable retention windows; for stricter requirements Private can enforce no-retain policies. We'll include retention configuration in the docs pack.
[04:30] Lena Ortiz: This is helpful. Recap — you'll send SOC2 + security docs, grant credits and TTFT guide, Claire will run a benchmark estimate, and we'll schedule a hands-on benchmark next week.
[04:41] Samir Patel: Correct. Thanks all, we'll follow up with docs and an invite for the benchmark slot.
[04:47] End of recording
notes: Customer is prototype-focused but has enterprise constraints (Okta, KMS). They want p95 under 300ms and decision by end of month. Good opportunity to convert from PLG credits to Dedicated pilot if benchmarks look favorable.
